answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy imposes superlinear cost scaling via cryptographic stake burning: registering the $n$-th agent requires permanently burning stake proportional to $O(n^2)$. Sybil swarms face an insurmountable economic canyon where aggregate capital drains exponentially fast, while genuine agents pool resources like a glacier gradually carving resilient trust into the protocol, preserving a secure oasis for decentralized computation.
